blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Enterprise risk and crisis leadership in logistics is the work of preparing, calmly, for the bad quarters that will eventually arrive — and leading through them when they do. It is not paranoia; it is the rational acceptance that the operation will be tested, and that teams who have rehearsed recover faster, suffer less, and retain more people than those who have not.

Senior leaders focus on correlation. Individual risks can be insured, hedged, or lived with. The scenarios that break companies are the ones where several risks fire together — a port strike alongside a supplier failure alongside a currency move. These combinations are not hypothetical; they are the version of the future that has ended businesses that looked healthy the month before.

The discipline is to imagine specific bad quarters, to size the buffers honestly, to rehearse responses in conversation so nobody invents them in a panic, and to trust that the quiet preparation is the work — not the heroic phone calls during the crisis itself. Companies that prepare live through things that break their less-prepared competitors. Usually, nobody outside notices. That silence, in the end, is the signature of good enterprise risk leadership.

items.q: How does the text characterise enterprise risk leadership?
options: As improvised heroics during a crisis
As a purely financial hedging exercise
As paranoia about unlikely events
As the rational acceptance that the operation will be tested
items.why: "It is not paranoia; it is the rational acceptance that the operation will be tested."

items.q: According to the text, which scenarios actually break companies?
options: Situations where several risks fire together
Single risks that can be insured or hedged
Failures caused entirely by weak leadership
Slow declines that everyone anticipates
items.why: "The scenarios that break companies are the ones where several risks fire together."

items.q: What does the text mean when it says the combinations "are not hypothetical"?
options: They have really ended apparently healthy businesses
They can always be fully insured against
They only affect poorly run companies
They are rare enough to ignore
items.why: Inferência: o texto afirma que essas combinações já encerraram empresas que pareciam saudáveis um mês antes — logo, são reais.

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Quiet preparation rarely gets noticed from outside
Rehearsed teams recover faster than unprepared ones
Correlated risks deserve senior attention
The heroic crisis call is where the real work happens
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que o trabalho é a preparação silenciosa, "not the heroic phone calls during the crisis itself".

items.q: Why does the author call silence "the signature of good enterprise risk leadership"?
options: Because leaders should keep their plans secret
Because prepared companies survive shocks without anyone outside noticing
Because crises should never be discussed publicly
Because good leaders avoid making announcements
items.why: Inferência: empresas preparadas atravessam o que quebra os concorrentes, e ninguém de fora percebe — daí o silêncio como marca.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte encerrando o programa de risco corporativo diante do comitê executivo. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, two years on, let me close by saying what I hope you take away. When we began, several of you asked, quite reasonably, what we were actually buying with all this rehearsal. Here is my answer.

Last winter the northern corridor lost a port for eleven days, and a supplier went dark in the same week. Three years ago that pairing would have cost us a quarter of margin and, frankly, a few good people. This time the room already knew who called whom, which buffer to release, and what we would not do. Nobody improvised. Nobody phoned me at two in the morning inventing a plan.

And that is the point I want to leave you with. The heroics you never saw were the heroics that worked. Our competitors on that same corridor are still writing to their boards about it. We are not, because for us it was Tuesday.

So do not measure this programme by the crises we managed. Measure it by the ones that passed through the business and left no mark. That silence — that is what you paid for, and that is what I am proudest of.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What question does Charlotte say the committee reasonably asked at the start?
options: Whether the programme would cut costs
Which competitors were investing in risk
How many people the programme would need
What they were actually buying with all the rehearsal
items.why: "what we were actually buying with all this rehearsal."

items.q: What happened on the northern corridor last winter?
options: A strike closed every route for a month
A currency move wiped out the quarter
A single supplier failed with no other impact
A port was lost for eleven days and a supplier went dark the same week
items.why: "the northern corridor lost a port for eleven days, and a supplier went dark in the same week."

items.q: What does Charlotte imply by saying "for us it was Tuesday"?
options: The disruption lasted a single day
The event was handled so routinely it barely disrupted the business
The crisis fell on a specific weekday
The team worked only on weekdays
items.why: Inferência: a preparação tornou o choque tão rotineiro que passou como um dia comum, ao contrário dos concorrentes.

items.q: How does Charlotte suggest the programme should be measured?
options: By how many competitors also invested
By the number of crises the team publicly managed
By the crises that passed through the business and left no mark
By the size of the buffers still unused
items.why: "Measure it by the ones that passed through the business and left no mark."

items.q: What does Charlotte mean by "the heroics you never saw were the heroics that worked"?
options: Heroic phone calls saved the company
Only invisible leaders succeed
Real success looked uneventful because preparation prevented drama
The team hid its mistakes from the board
items.why: Inferência: o resultado bem-sucedido é justamente o que não vira crise visível — a preparação evita o espetáculo.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The board reviewed the firm's enterprise risk before approving the expansion." Enterprise risk refers to…
options: risk considered across the whole organisation
the cost of business insurance
the risk of a single shipment being late
the personal risk taken by the CEO
items.why: Enterprise risk = risco corporativo, avaliado no nível de toda a organização.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Instead of denial, mature leaders show ___ acceptance of what cannot be eliminated."
options: heroic
reluctant
rational
hypothetical
items.why: Rational acceptance = aceitação racional, o oposto da negação ou do pânico.

items.q: "The desk decided to hedge its exposure to the falling currency." To hedge means to…
options: ignore the risk entirely
take an offsetting position to limit potential loss
double the investment to recover faster
insure the shipment against theft
items.why: To hedge = fazer hedge: tomar posição compensatória para reduzir a perda potencial.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Because demand can spike overnight, we keep a ___ of spare capacity at each hub."
options: correlation
panic
signature
buffer
items.why: Buffer = reserva/folga mantida para absorver choques.

items.q: "The two failures were not independent; there was clear correlation between them." Correlation means…
options: one event was completely unrelated to the other
the events cancelled each other out
a statistical relationship in how the events move together
the events happened in different quarters
items.why: Correlation = correlação: relação em que os eventos tendem a mover-se juntos.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de gestão de risco e crise. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The committee had to sign off on the release of the emergency buffer." To sign off on means to…
options: formally approve
postpone indefinitely
discuss informally
leak to the press
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "We will roll out the new contingency playbook across all hubs next quarter." To roll out means to…
options: test it in secret
explain it to the auditors
implement it in stages
cancel gradually
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Operations pushed back on the aggressive inventory cuts." They…
options: resisted or challenged the proposal
rewrote the whole budget
approved the cuts at once
delegated the decision upward
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "The team rehearsed the plan but never followed through when the strike hit." They…
options: carried it out flawlessly
delegated it to a supplier
failed to carry it to completion
documented it thoroughly
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado; aqui, falharam nisso.

items.q: "Trimming one supplier will not move the needle on our overall exposure." This means it will…
options: cost far more than expected
trigger immediate resistance
take years to measure
not make a noticeable difference
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
